title: Knee Collateral and Posterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries

differentials.name: ACL rupture
differentials.key: Pop, rapid haemarthrosis, giving way, positive Lachman

differentials.name: Tibial plateau fracture
differentials.key: Ottawa positive, unable to bear weight

differentials.name: Patellar dislocation
differentials.key: Medial knee pain after twisting, apprehension

differentials.name: Knee dislocation
differentials.key: Multiple ligament laxity, often spontaneously reduced

qa: Why test valgus at 0 and 30 degrees? Opening at 30 isolates the MCL; opening at 0 indicates additional structures are injured.
Which muscle group is prioritised in PCL rehab? Quadriceps.
What is the sag sign? Backward sag of the tibia with hips and knees at 90 degrees.
Why check pulses with multi-ligament laxity? Knee dislocation can injure the popliteal artery.
Name a sign of peroneal nerve injury. Weak ankle dorsiflexion (foot drop) and numbness of the dorsum of the foot.

fields.Position: Supine; knee at 0 then 20 to 30 degrees flexion
fields.Action: Stabilise the thigh, push the knee inward with a hand on the lateral knee, other hand pulls the ankle outward
fields.Meaning: Gapping at 30 degrees: MCL; gapping also at 0 degrees: MCL plus cruciate or capsule involvement
LCL; at 0 degrees suggests combined injury

fields.Positive: Increased posterior translation, soft end feel

fields.Position: Supine, hips and knees at 90 degrees, legs supported at the heels
fields.Positive: Tibia sags back compared with the other side

fields.Action: Externally rotate both feet; compare thigh-foot angle
fields.Meaning: Posterolateral corner (30 only) or PCL plus PLC (30 and 90) [Ref – to verify]

redFlags.Finding: Laxity of several ligaments, high-energy trauma
Calf swelling and pain during rehabilitation

manualNotes: Typical return to sport: grade I MCL a few weeks; grade II longer; grade III and PCL longer still [Ref – to verify]. Base return on criteria, not time alone.
modalityNotes: Ice and compression early. Measure effusion, range, valgus stress pain, quadriceps strength (limb symmetry), hop tests, IKDC or KOOS.
